items.text: The fuel price caps continue: the Energy Minister published new maximum prices valid from Nov 10 — petrol 95 at 6.04 zł/l, petrol 98 at 6.67 zł/l and diesel at 7.74 zł/l, all lower than the previous caps. Some outlets printed different figures; these are the numbers in the PAP Biznes summary.

items.text: The złoty firmed on the first trading day after S&P cut Poland's outlook to negative: EUR/PLN fell below 4.39 (reference 4.3947) as the dollar weakened. S&P also moved Bank Pekao's outlook to negative after the sovereign action.

items.notes: Federal Register notice not yet seen; status of the 178 product exclusions unconfirmed. Updates W-261108-01.
items.text: Trade press reports that the US has formalised a two-month extension of its suspension of Section 301 port fees on China-linked vessels (USTR had proposed running it to Jan 9, 2027). China said it is extending, by two months, its suspension of the extra 24% tariff on US goods and its special port fees; its 10% tariff stays.

Delhi's official 24-hour AQI for Nov 9, the day after Diwali, was 344 ('very poor'); missing monitoring data mean the true figure may be higher (HT estimated about 360). GRAP Stage III, in force since Nov 6, stays; no move to Stage IV. Forecasters expect 'very poor' air on Nov 10-11 and no rain until Nov 15.

After meeting Qatar's prime minister and VP Vance at the White House, Trump said the war with Iran is "effectively" over militarily and the US would keep the status quo, including the naval blockade and the Iron Gate land blockade, while staying ready to strike. Qatar's PM reportedly passed on an Iranian two-day proposal on Hormuz security.

Secretary of State Rubio said there has been no real progress in talks and called some of Iran's demands unrealistic. Iran's foreign ministry said Washington must end sanctions, the blockade and the war on all fronts before negotiations; a senior security official dismissed talk of talks as fake. Accounts from the two sides conflict.

US forces struck Qeshm Island (confirmed by Iran's Tasnim), and Iran said another tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The Pentagon puts US military deaths since late February at 23; Trump said none had been lost.

Stocks rallied as oil fell on hopes the Iran war is winding down: the S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7,549.94, the Dow 2.15% (+1,104 points) to 52,389.75 and the Nasdaq 2.74%. Brent fell 5.85% to $92.57 and WTI 4.38% to $86.85. The 10-year Treasury yield edged up to about 4.87% before the October CPI; fed funds futures priced about an 84% chance of a December rate hike.

Nvidia is investigating CEO Jensen Huang after he acknowledged a relationship with a business executive whom US intelligence reportedly judged was gathering information for China. The board says it has no reason to believe national-security or company secrets were compromised; China called the claims smears. Shares fell about 4-5%.

items.notes: No newer count found. Relates to W-261106-02.
items.text: Mississippi Senate race: Nov 10 is the deadline for voters who cast affidavit ballots for lack of photo ID to cure them; counties must certify by Nov 13. Colom's last reported lead was 2,574 votes (AP, Nov 6). Republicans have demanded affidavit ballots be segregated and preserved, signalling a possible legal challenge.
House Republicans hold their leadership election today (Scalise v. Jordan for minority leader in the next Congress); both made final pitches on Nov 9.
Registered unemployment was 5.8% in October (preliminary), unchanged from September and in line with forecasts. GUS said the average gross wage in Q3 rose 6.2% year on year to 9,317 zł.

items.thread: Poland public finances and credit ratings
items.text: Finance Minister Domański said the ministry will decide by the end of November whether Poland seeks additional loans from the EU's SAFE defence programme, and that Poland wants defence funding in the next EU budget.
Senators may submit candidates for two new Monetary Policy Council (RPP) members from Nov 9 until noon on Nov 25.

Coal miner JSW signed a loan of up to 1.07bn zł with the state Industrial Development Agency (ARP), running to 2038, covering a 400m zł advance under a preliminary share-sale deal and restructuring financing.

items.notes: Details not confirmed from Operational Command.
items.text: Russia attacked Ukraine again overnight; the Government Security Centre (RCB) sent alerts to residents of eastern Poland, according to TVP Info’s daily summary. No airspace violation was reported in the sources checked.

The attacker, 24-year-old Michał O. from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, died in a Kraków hospital at about 4:30 am on Nov 9 after three operations, so he will never be charged. His autopsy is scheduled for Nov 10.

Prosecutors said his parents and sister were found shot dead in the family flat in Ostrowiec; a preliminary assessment puts their deaths before the attack. That brings the toll to nine dead. Interior Minister Kierwiński says he had no record and acted alone; prosecutors are still checking whether anyone helped and found no obvious symbolism in his room.

Thousands joined the silent march on Monday evening, led by Mayor Gibała with President Nawrocki and PM Tusk walking together; there were no speeches. Nawrocki later awarded the two wounded police officers the Officer’s Cross of Polonia Restituta, and the city council plans honorary citizenship for them.
Fifteen people remain injured; 14 are stable. One wounded officer is still serious, the other stable, and both have regained consciousness.

items.notes: Updates W-261108-07; Basilica status and 11 Nov ceremony programme not found.
items.text: Radio Kraków reports Rynek Główny has reopened. City mourning lasts to Nov 11; the city plans retractable barriers around the square and police are weighing vehicle restrictions for Independence Day. The condolence book at City Hall stays open until Nov 11.
